sources.quote: Upper bounds: Mahler 1953 (42), Mignotte 1974 (20), Chudnovsky, Hata 1993 (8.0161), Salikhov 2008 (7.6063), Zeilberger-Zudilin 2020 (7.103205334137, arXiv:1912.06345)
For every nu > 2 there is Q(nu) such that |pi - p/q| >= q^{-nu} for all integers p and all q >= Q(nu); hence the irrationality exponent mu(pi) = 2 (the threshold is ineffective).
The 23-page proof is not a better Hata/Salikhov integral: it is a Roth-style interpolation-determinant argument

steps: Suppose pi had unusually good fraction approximations
Use several of them to build a nonzero determinant
Whole-number reasons keep it big; analysis makes it tiny

voice.text: Bounds fell from forty-two to about seven. The claim jumps straight to two.
Too-good fractions for pi would build a determinant both nonzero and too small.
Claimed: two, the least any irrational has.
